class_examples.label: illegal_turn
class_examples.caption: A car from the main road drives deep into the junction and makes a U-shaped turn back onto the lower street: the forbidden route (the allowed right turn is right after the far crossing).

class_examples.label: red_light
class_examples.caption: A vehicle crosses the stop line while the signal for its approach is red.

class_examples.label: stopped_vehicle
class_examples.caption: A lone car stands on the junction for more than 10 s, not packed in a queue: stopping on the junction is an event even if the car leaves with the next green phase.

class_examples.label: congestion
class_examples.caption: The junction jams: a dense block of cars stands for longer than one signal phase. An ordinary red-light queue is not congestion; it clears on green.

class_examples.label: jaywalking
class_examples.caption: Pedestrians leave the zebra and cut across the asphalt towards the near crossing.

class_examples.label: stop_line
class_examples.caption: At dusk a car stops on red past the stop line, its front on the far zebra, and waits there for the green instead of behind the line.

failures.title: False alarm: pedestrian on the island
failures.explanation: Part B raises a 0.5 s alarm (risk 0.52), the only one on the samples, for a pedestrian standing on the traffic island while a car passes. Distances are measured in image space, and perspective squeezes the gap between the island and the lane.

failures.title: Close following read as a near conflict
failures.explanation: Two cars in the far lane, one closing in on the other in slow traffic. The risk curve peaks at 0.45 here, below the 0.5 alarm line but the highest value of the clip, although nothing dangerous happens. Distances are measured in image space: on the far side of the junction perspective squeezes a normal following gap into a few pixels. A ground-plane (bird's-eye) projection with metric gaps is the fix we would try.

failures.title: Jaywalking or a desire line?
failures.explanation: Almost every pedestrian phase, people step off the far zebra and cut diagonally across the asphalt to the near crossing. By the definition it is jaywalking and we report it; if the annotators treat this habitual path as normal, these events are false positives.

failures.title: A lone stop merged into a whole-video segment
failures.explanation: A car with hazard lights stands for minutes near the bus stop. Same-class events that overlap must be merged into one segment, so this stop swallows the shorter stops around it and the video gets one long stopped_vehicle segment instead of several short ones.
